# Blind reader, task S: did three runs make the same questions of the same news? (read-only)

Repository `/Users/lchingen/hivemind`. Read ONLY `docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-3/july-topics-packet.json`.
Open no other file: keys and other readers' answers exist and you must not see them. Do not edit files or run model calls.

A research system read the same fourteen days of news about one company (NVIDIA) three times, independently (runs X, Y, Z),
each time starting with no questions. The packet holds the 40 topics the three runs opened. Each item: `run`; `topic` (the
topic as first written: `description`, `outcome`, `period`, `opens_as`, `settled_by`); `opening_article` (date, title); and
`attempts`: three independent attempts to turn the topic into one judged question, each either the `question` with `whose`
(the company's ticker or a theme id), its `due_day` and its `answer_choices`, or `declined` with the reason.

**1. Group the topics by matter**: the same underlying thing in the news (for example one deal, one product's launch, one
price, one regulator's proceeding), whichever run opened it and however it is worded.

**2. For every matter that two or three runs opened**, compare the judged questions across runs (use each topic's first
attempt; say so where a topic's own attempts disagree with each other). Verdict, one of:
- `same`: the same thing is measured or asked, for the same period or by the same deadline, so one real-world outcome gives
  the same answer in each run (differences of wording or of a few range edges do not count);
- `one_apart`: two runs the same, one different;
- `different`: the runs ask different things, or some run has no judged question (declined in at least two of its three
  attempts).
For `one_apart` and `different`, say **what differs**, from this closed list (several allowed): `what_is_measured`,
`period_or_deadline`, `whose_question` (company or which theme), `several_parts` (one topic asks two things), `no_question`
(declined), `answer_choices` (the ranges are far apart). And say in one sentence whether the difference could change the
answer a reader gets.

**3. For every topic**: `answerable` (yes, no, unsure: as written in its first attempt, can public material settle it on its
due day?) and `worth_tracking` (yes, no, unsure: would an analyst covering this company hold a view on it, because it can
change the company's revenue, profit, cash or credit risk?), each with a reason of at most 15 words.

Return, as your final message and nothing else, JSON lines:
- one line per matter: `{"matter": "<short name>", "topics": ["t..", ...], "runs": ["X", ...], "verdict": "same|one_apart|different|one_run_only", "differs": [...], "changes_the_answer": "yes|no|unsure", "why": "<= 30 words"}`
- then one line per topic: `{"id": "t..", "answerable": "...", "worth_tracking": "...", "why": "<= 15 words"}`
# Blind reader, task K: is each topic's yardstick stated in the news, or did someone have to choose it? (read-only)

Repository `/Users/lchingen/hivemind`. Read ONLY `docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-3/july-topics-as-opened.json`.
Open no other file: keys and other readers' answers exist and you must not see them. Do not edit files or run model calls.

The file holds 40 research topics a system opened while reading news about one company (NVIDIA). Each has the topic as it
was written (`description`: the question; `outcome`: what is tracked; `period`; `opens_as`; `settled_by`) and the date and title
of the article it was opened from. You do not see the articles or what was done with the topics later.

To judge a topic later, one needs a yardstick: **what exactly is measured or which event, and for which period or by which
day**. For each topic, say where its yardstick comes from, as far as the topic's own fields show:

- `stated`: the topic takes both from something fixed outside the writer's choice: a date or period the company, an authority
  or the report itself gives; a figure a company publishes for a fixed period (an annual report line, a calendar-year total);
  one named decision or one named product's shipment.
- `chosen`: the writer had to choose at least one of them, and another reasonable writer could have chosen otherwise. Name
  what was chosen, from this closed list (several allowed): `what_is_measured` (for example a price with no single published
  series; an average, a level or a direction), `period_or_deadline` (no stated date, a rolling window, a deadline set by a
  default), `which_part` (the topic holds two or more things, or several actors, and one must be picked), `whose_bucket`
  (it is unclear whether it is the company's matter or a wider theme's).

Also mark `parts`: 1 when the topic asks one thing, 2 or more when its question or its tracked outcome names several things
that could each be tracked.

Return, as your final message and nothing else, one JSON object per line, in the file's order:
`{"id": "t..", "yardstick": "stated|chosen", "chosen": [...], "parts": 1, "why": "<= 20 words"}`

The statement under test: the system forms a steady, answerable question when the news hands it one thing with its date or
its yearly report, and does not when someone has to choose the yardstick (what is measured, the period or deadline, which
part, whose matter).

Readings: task S (did the runs ask the same question; two families) and task K (is each topic's yardstick stated or chosen;
two families who do not see the judged questions). A topic counts as "stated" or "chosen" only where both families say so;
the others are "split" and reported apart. A matter is "stated" when all its topics are, "chosen" when any of its topics is
chosen by both families.

- **P1, the three July runs, by matter.** Among the matters that two or three runs opened, the share that task S calls
  `same` (both families) is at least 50 points higher for stated matters than for chosen ones. A gap under 25 points, or

- **P2, the three July runs, by topic.** Of the topics declined in at least two of three attempts (9 by code), at least 8 are
  chosen; of the stated topics, at most one in ten is declined in at least two attempts.

  three attempts are all chosen; no stated topic is declined in two attempts. With three declined topics this is a weak
  test; it can refute, it cannot establish.
- **What refutes the statement:** P1's gap under 25 points; or more than two of the nine declined July topics stated; or a
  stated topic declined twice in the later weeks.
- **What it cannot show even if all three hold:** that a rule for the yardstick would fix it; that the questions lost matter
  to a final answer; a rate.

# Claude's own read of the three July runs' questions, stored before any reader's answer (2026-11-15)

Read from the packet with the key: each topic's judged question and answer choices in its three attempts.

**A correction to my own reflection first.** I wrote that the cloud companies' 2026 spending came out as a figure, a figure
with a threshold and a yes-or-no. That is true of the topics as the first step worded them. The judged questions are the same
in all three runs: the big four's combined data-center capital spending for calendar 2026, due 2027-03-31, with the same five
ranges. The answer-choice step brought three wordings to one question. My "same news, different questions" was read off the
wrong layer and is too broad.

## Matters and what the runs made of them (judged questions, first attempt unless said)

| Matter | Runs | Same judged question? | What differs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vera Rubin first shipments by the end of 2026 | 3 | same | wording only |
| The big four's capital spending in 2026 | 3 | same | nothing (one attempt's ranges) |
| Supply and purchase commitments in the next annual report | 3 | same | ranges a little |
| The French competition inquiry's decision by the fiscal year-end | 3 | same | wording only |
| China's permission for H200 sales | 3 | two same, one different | one run asks whether Nvidia records China revenue from H200, a later event and the company's own |
| The Kyber rack's first shipments | 3 | two same, one different | by the end of 2028 in two runs, during 2027 in one |
| Credit support and guarantees to cloud partners | 3 | same quantity, different date | "signed by 2027-12-31" in one run, "in the FY2027 annual report" in two; ranges guessed and far apart |
| The H100 rental price | 3 | different | declined in 6 of 9 attempts; a yearly average once, a year-end price once, a yes-or-no under another theme once |
| Memory contract prices | 3 | different | declined in two runs (a rolling year; two things); two figure questions in the third |
| The China domestic-share survey | 2 | same (no question) | declined in 5 of 6 attempts |
| The Intel stake | 2 | different | declined in one run, a figure in the other |
| Federal AI obligations | 2 | different | declined in one run, a figure in the other |
| Opened by one run only | | | the DeepSeek inquiry, 2027 capital spending, Firmus, custom-chip spending, the Vera CPU, the U.S. approval of China sales |

Shared by two or three runs: 12 matters. The same judged question wherever opened: 4, and a fifth consistently without one.
One run apart: 3. Different: 4.

## The pattern I see, to be tested by readers who do not know it

The four stable matters are ones where the news hands over one thing with its date or its yearly report: a shipment the
company dates, a regulator's decision, a figure in the annual report, a calendar-year total with a stated plan. Every unstable
one is a matter where someone has to choose the yardstick: for a market price, what is measured, over which period and under
which theme; for an event with no stated date, the deadline; for a matter with several actors or parts, which one; and
whether a small matter is worth a question at all. By my own sorting: given, 4 of 4 the same; chosen, 0 of 7.

If readers sorting the topics by "stated or chosen" without seeing the judged questions do not reproduce that split, the
pattern is mine and not the record's.

# Are the eleven first-pass refusals reachable? Two blind readers, $0 (D476), 2026-11-13

**Answer: of the eleven theses the judge's first pass refused on the full run, both readers agree on ten. Six should be declined: no
question worth asking in any shape the ladder step can take (five distinct matters). Four runs, two distinct matters, have a question
worth asking that the article supports in a shape that can be laddered: the H100 rental price (twice, from one article) and the memory
price (two articles). They split on one: federal AI obligations.** On this population Stage A counts 32 right, 22 by a written ladder,
of 40 (line scaled to 32 and 26). So the written line is reachable on paper only if all four agreed conversions land and nothing else is
lost: +4 gives 26.

Readers: Codex (`codex-phase1.jsonl`, `codex-phase2.jsonl`) and a Claude subagent (`claude-phase1.jsonl`, `claude-phase2.jsonl`). Each read
the article and the library at that step first, without the thesis, and wrote the questions the source supports (Codex 13, Claude 18:
12 distinct matters), then compared them with the thesis (`packet-phase2.json`); the key (`key.json`) was not shown.

| case | thesis | Codex | Claude | the mechanism behind the refusal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 5 | c1/clean-12, c3/clean-10: the H100 GPU-hour rental price in 2026 | reachable (as written for c1) | reachable (year-end price) | the ladder step's rule "a matter no listed theme covers" (`poc/universe.json` holds 12 themes, among them "AI capital spending" and "Semiconductor cycle"; the model judged that none covers a GPU rental price, and the Stage A readers split): not the thesis's shape |

**What it shows.**
1. Most refusals are right, and for a reason upstream of the ladder: four of the six right refusals are theses Step 1 should not have
   opened at all (a completed stake, a small stake, a background sentence, an outcome with no settling material). The refusal is the

   H100 refusals right on the theme list as it stands (council round 5).

## Addendum: every theme-coverage decline in the stored final-configuration answers (council round 20's step 1, $0; `theme-census.txt`)

Read: the fourth Stage A run (132 answers) and the full run's three draws (120), every send. **Six theses were declined for "no listed theme
covers it" (12 sends), and the same model laddered three of them under an existing theme in other sends.** The H100 rental price: declined
in five of nine sends over the three draws and laddered in four: three under "Semiconductor cycle" (an annual average or a year-end price)
and one under "Custom silicon at cloud providers" as a yes/no on staying below the peak (c2 send 3; council round 21 caught the miscount). The other three:
a US lidar ban (two declines, once laddered under "Chip export controls", a wrong fit), the CPU-to-GPU ratio in inference (declined 3 of 3),
Huawei's chip output (two declines). 31 theses were laddered under a theme in 80 sends; memory prices go to "Semiconductor cycle" every time,
although that theme's definition (`poc/universe.json`) watches only industry revenue growth.

So the H100 refusal is not a missing theme or a new-theme path: it is the model's coin flip on whether a thinly defined existing theme
"covers" a market price, the same theme it stretches to memory prices without hesitation. A new-theme design (storage, deduplication,
cross-company reading, D191) is not needed to explain it; whether a theme's definition should name the prices it carries is a product
question about `poc/universe.json`, which production shares.

"""The tally of the blind review of the stored runs' questions against the predictions registered beforehand ($0).

  python3 tally_review.py <key folder outside the repository>
"""
import collections
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = Path('/Users/lchingen/hivemind')
DATA = ROOT / 'poc/data'
FAMILIES = ('codex', 'claude')


def lines_of(path):
    rows = []
    for line in Path(path).read_text().splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith('{'):
            rows.append(json.loads(line))
    return rows


def kinds_of(name):
    """{topic id: 'stated' | 'chosen' | 'split'} from the two families' task K answers, with each family's own answer."""
    by_family = {family: {row['id']: row for row in lines_of(HERE / f'{family}-{name}.jsonl')} for family in FAMILIES}
    out = {}
    for topic in by_family['codex']:
        marks = [by_family[family][topic]['yardstick'] for family in FAMILIES]
        out[topic] = marks[0] if marks[0] == marks[1] else 'split'
    return out, by_family


def declined_twice(attempts):
    return sum(1 for attempt in attempts if 'declined' in attempt) >= 2


def main(keys):
    keys = Path(keys)
    key = json.loads((keys / 'july-topics-key.json').read_text())
    packet = {item['id']: item for item in json.loads((HERE / 'july-topics-packet.json').read_text())}
    kind, kind_rows = kinds_of('stated-or-chosen')
    print('JULY, 40 topics. Yardstick by both families:', dict(collections.Counter(kind.values())),
          '| families agree on', sum(1 for value in kind.values() if value != 'split'), 'of', len(kind))
    declined = {topic: declined_twice(item['attempts']) for topic, item in packet.items()}
    table = collections.Counter((kind[topic], declined[topic]) for topic in packet)
    print('P2. declined in at least two of three attempts, by yardstick:')
    for name in ('stated', 'chosen', 'split'):
        total = table[(name, True)] + table[(name, False)]
        print(f'     {name}: {table[(name, True)]} of {total} declined twice')
    declined_topics = [topic for topic in packet if declined[topic]]
    print('     the declined topics:', [(key[topic], kind[topic]) for topic in declined_topics])
    print('P1. shared matters, by each family\'s own grouping in task S:')
    for family in FAMILIES:
        rows = [row for row in lines_of(HERE / f'{family}-same-question.jsonl') if 'matter' in row]
        shared = [row for row in rows if len(set(row['runs'])) >= 2]
        tally = collections.Counter()
        listing = []
        for row in shared:
            marks = [kind.get(topic, 'split') for topic in row['topics']]
            matter_kind = 'chosen' if 'chosen' in marks else 'stated' if all(mark == 'stated' for mark in marks) else 'split'
            tally[(matter_kind, row['verdict'])] += 1
            listing.append((row['matter'][:44], matter_kind, row['verdict'], ','.join(row.get('differs', []))[:60]))
        print(f'   {family}: {len(rows)} matters, {len(shared)} shared by two or three runs; one-run-only {sum(1 for row in rows if len(set(row["runs"])) < 2)}')
        for name in ('stated', 'chosen', 'split'):
            total = sum(count for (matter_kind, _), count in tally.items() if matter_kind == name)
            same = tally[(name, 'same')]
            print(f'        {name}: same {same} of {total}' + (f' ({100 * same // total}%)' if total else ''), {verdict: count for (matter_kind, verdict), count in tally.items() if matter_kind == name})
        for entry in listing:
            print('           ', entry)
    topic_rows = {family: {row['id']: row for row in lines_of(HERE / f'{family}-same-question.jsonl') if 'id' in row} for family in FAMILIES}
    for field in ('answerable', 'worth_tracking'):
        both = collections.Counter()
        for topic in packet:
            marks = [topic_rows[family].get(topic, {}).get(field, 'missing') for family in FAMILIES]
            both[marks[0] if marks[0] == marks[1] else 'split'] += 1
        print(f'{field} (both families):', dict(both))
    unworthy = [key[topic] for topic in packet if all(topic_rows[family].get(topic, {}).get('worth_tracking') == 'no' for family in FAMILIES)]
    print('topics both families call not worth tracking:', unworthy, '| of them declined twice:', [key[t] for t in packet if declined[t] and key[t] in unworthy])
    later = HERE / 'codex-stated-or-chosen-later-weeks.jsonl'
    if later.exists() and (HERE / 'claude-stated-or-chosen-later-weeks.jsonl').exists():
        later_key = json.loads((keys / 'later-weeks-key.json').read_text())
        later_kind, _ = kinds_of('stated-or-chosen-later-weeks')
        attempts = {}
        for name, folder in (('week 09-22', DATA / 'clean-lean-week-2026-11-14/week-r2/c1'), ('week 10-06', DATA / 'clean-second-week-2026-11-15/week-continued/c1')):
            for send in sorted((folder / 'ladder').glob('send-*')):
                for line in (send / 'outcomes.jsonl').read_text().splitlines():
                    row = json.loads(line)
                    attempts.setdefault(f"{name} {row['case']}", []).append(row['status'] != 'ladder')
        print('\nP3, HELD OUT: the two later weeks, 20 topics. Yardstick by both families:', dict(collections.Counter(later_kind.values())))
        table = collections.Counter((later_kind[topic], sum(attempts[later_key[topic]]) >= 2) for topic in later_kind)
        for name in ('stated', 'chosen', 'split'):
            total = table[(name, True)] + table[(name, False)]
            print(f'     {name}: {table[(name, True)]} of {total} declined twice')
        print('     the declined topics:', [(later_key[topic], later_kind[topic]) for topic in later_kind if sum(attempts[later_key[topic]]) >= 2])
        print('     declined at least once:', [(later_key[topic], later_kind[topic], sum(attempts[later_key[topic]])) for topic in later_kind if sum(attempts[later_key[topic]]) >= 1])

**The system often cannot turn important news into a question that can be answered and followed, and we have not established how much of that problem a real starting research library would remove.**

For example, the July runs treated the H100 rental price differently: one produced a question and two declined it. The runs also disagreed about Kyber’s deadline. Those are different kinds of loss, even though both occur between reading news and delivering a usable question.

1. **Your statement is directionally right, but several clauses are stronger than the evidence.**

- **Empty notebook:** D469 chose an empty start provisionally for the frozen-window measurement. It did **not** decide that the product always starts empty. Nor does the evidence show that empty starts caused the failures. A real prior library remains untested as a remedy. [D469](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md)

- **“Not settled for most matters in real news”:** Task K’s readers did not see the articles. They judged what the *topic fields* indicated; they cannot establish what the news itself stated. Their sorting also did not distinguish stable from unstable questions under the registered prediction. [Task K brief](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-3/brief-stated-or-chosen.md), [predictions and tallies](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-3/tally-output.txt)

- **“Choice of what to follow is mostly sound”:** I would not say this. The two readers called 30 of 40 topics worth tracking, but saw titles and topics rather than the source articles or the existing library. An earlier source-first review found the Intel stake and Firmus investment should have been declined; in this review the readers split on them. The new count is a lead, not a source-checked verdict. [Blind responses](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-3/claude-same-question.jsonl), [earlier source review](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/e2e-comparison-2026-11-13/reachability/RESULT.md)

- **“3 of 12 shared matters the same”:** That is the readers’ tally, but it combines different outcomes. The China domestic-share matter was declined in both runs’ first attempts and at least twice in each; the brief classified a refusal as “different.” It is consistently **unanswered**, not evidence that two delivered questions differed. We should report missing questions and differing delivered questions separately. [Task S brief](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-3/brief-same-question.md), [reader responses](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/reflection-3/codex-same-question.jsonl)

- **“12 of 31 answerable”:** Both readers said yes to 12; they said no to 2, were both unsure on 10 and split on 7. The other 19 are not established unanswerable. Their assessments were not checked against actual public settling material.

- **“Each run fills the gap its own way”:** Some differences are demonstrated; their common cause is not. A wrong or unstable question and a refusal under a written rule can arise from different mechanisms. The later steps inherit what they receive, but the answer-choice step also sometimes improves the topic—as it did for the 2026 cloud-spending question.

I therefore see **two connected failures, not one proven mechanism**: worthwhile matters can receive no question, and delivered questions can ask materially different or unresolvable things. Both support the broader product problem. Neither proves that the standard’s open choices or the empty start caused most losses.

2. **“The loop cannot close without Alex” is too strong.**

D439 authorizes the council, while Alex is inactive, to decide and test within its limits. It could legitimately perform a source-first, $0 review of the stored refused and delivered questions against the decisions already in force. It could also test, without changing a frozen piece, whether a dated real library can be reconstructed without future information.

A concrete falsifier for the first review: if the apparently worthwhile missing questions are unsupported by their articles or already covered by an existing question, the claimed product loss shrinks. Such work would change the picture without requiring a new product rule.

What the council **cannot infer** is that Alex has chosen a permanent starting library, endorsed new rules for the three open shapes, or approved changes to the frozen ruler. He is reachable now, so D466’s outstanding choices can be brought to him; that is different from saying no useful investigation is possible without him.

3. **Recommendation and test**

I would **not** ask Alex to rule on eight cards and convert those rulings into a general shape rule. That is several choices, and it risks fitting the product to this window. The cards also need source passages and the existing-library context before he can judge them fairly.

My recommendation is one framing choice:

> **For the next product comparison, should we include a real research library that existed before the test period, alongside the empty-start results already collected? I recommend yes, if we can reconstruct it with sources and dates and without using future information.**

This adds a comparison condition; it does not replace the frozen reference, change an existing gate, or assume that the system stops proposing questions. The three specific shape concerns should remain concerns until a source-backed review shows a product decision is needed.

**The one test after his answer:** at $0, reconstruct one real library as it stood before a later stored news window, and trace the stored important matters against that library and the articles in date order. Compare what was already covered, what still needed a new question, and what could be answered. The test fails as a basis for comparison if the library’s prior existence, sources or dates cannot be verified, or if the reconstruction needs information from after the starting date. It measures feasibility and coverage, not whether a live system would perform better; a paid comparison would need its own design.

We agree on the product problem and on stopping the cycle of local wording fixes. We do **not** yet agree that the open product rules and empty start explain the problem, or that eight card rulings should become a new general rule.

CONSENSUS: no, because the proposed cause and the proposed owner decision go beyond what the stored evidence establishes.
